_comment: Hand-maintained observation of what the registries actually serve today. This is NOT proof evidence: nothing here is generated, and nothing here asserts that a pair works. It exists because a pair can be superseded on the registry while its proof stays perfectly valid, and recommending a superseded pair can be actively harmful even when its evidence is sound. Update this file when a publish lands, then run: npm run compatibility:generate
reason: The Phase 10 unified-surface train (D-118, D-123/D-124/D-125) replaced the evidenced 0.2.3/0.4.3 pair, and the Phase 12 fixes (D-129) superseded it again with 0.5.0/0.8.0. The evidence for the older pair remains valid and is retained; it is simply no longer the pair a user should install.
hazard: Do not install visp-kit@0.2.3 while visp-hyper-agent@0.8.0 is present. visp-kit@0.2.3 declares the `visp` binary that visp-hyper-agent now provides, so whichever installs last silently wins the name.

provenance.phase12Local: conformance 11/11, golden path 6/6, cross-generation 4/4 — Linux only, local, against 0.4.0/0.7.0
provenance.note: NO evidence exists yet for the CURRENTLY SERVED pair 0.5.0/0.8.0. The Phase 12 runs covered 0.4.0/0.7.0, which the fixes have now superseded, and they were Linux-only and local. A recommendation requires one green CI run over BOTH platforms against identical artifacts of the served pair, plus an owner review of that run.
